before: Adds Idaho Code 61-335, titled 'New Large Load and Ratepayer Protection.' Defines a 'new large load' as a service-entrance load increase of 50 MW or more within a rolling 60-month period under a contract entered on or after 2026-07-01 (squarely covers data centers). Requires a PUC-approved service contract before a utility may serve such a load, including a commission 'no harm test'; makes the new large load responsible for its full cost of service (generation, transmission, substation, distribution); bars load-splitting to evade the threshold; requires financial security against stranded costs; and directs the commission to review rates in each general rate case to keep other ratepayers' bills from rising because of the new load.
after: Idaho Code 61-335 establishes a new large-load utility framework: a service entrance must have an increase in cumulative power requirement of at least 50 MW in any consecutive 60-month period and a public-utility contract entered on or after July 1, 2026. The increase is maximum contracted demand relative to the entrance’s highest contracted demand in the previous 60 months. The law requires commission-approved contracts and a no-harm test, full cost assignment, anti-evasion measures, financial security and rate-case review; data centers qualify only when the statutory criteria are met.
